transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because I’ve been having these thoughts that are hard to shake. I know that probably sounds a little ordinary, like everyone double-checks things, but for me it’s gotten… pretty upsetting.

I’ll think maybe I missed something important, like a wrong number in a data release, or that I left the back door unlocked, or paid a bill from the wrong account. Even if I’ve already checked, my mind keeps going back to it, like, “What if you caused something really bad?” And I can usually tell it doesn’t make sense, but I can’t seem to let it go.
Do you find yourself doing specific actions over and over to try to calm these thoughts?

Yes… I do. I mean, I try to keep it reasonable, but it doesn’t always stay that way.

If I’m worried about work, I’ll reopen spreadsheets and go through them again, or reread emails line by line to make sure I didn’t miss something. At home I check the locks, and with bills I’ll keep looking at the payment confirmation. I kind of do it in a certain order, like if I don’t, it doesn’t feel settled or… safe, I guess.

I know that probably sounds excessive. Some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, and I haven’t really finished anything because I’ve just been checking. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like doing these checks helps to reduce your anxiety about the thoughts you're having?

Yes… for a little while, I think it does. Or at least it makes me feel like I’ve done something to prevent the bad thing from happening.

Like if I reopen the spreadsheet or reread an email line by line, there’s this moment where I can breathe a bit easier. Same with checking the lock or the payment confirmation. But it has to be in the right order, or it doesn’t really feel finished… or safe, I guess.

I know that probably sounds like too much. It’s just that if I don’t do it, the anxiety gets really loud. And some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, checking and rechecking, and somehow nothing is actually finished.
Do you feel anxious when you're not having these specific thoughts about potential mistakes or dangers?

I’m not totally sure. I mean… I think I’m generally a bit tense, but I notice it the most when one of those worries comes up.

When I’m not thinking about a specific mistake or danger, I wouldn’t say I’m always panicking or anything. It’s more like I can be okay for a while, and then if something reminds me of it, the anxiety kind of snaps back into focus. Does that answer what you mean?
Are you generally anxious even when you're not thinking about those specific worries?

I don’t think so… not in the same way, anyway.

I mean, I can be a little keyed up just generally, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. It’s mostly when one of those specific worries gets going that it really feels like anxiety. If I’m not thinking about them, I can sometimes feel pretty normal, I guess.

Is that… is that the kind of distinction you’re asking about?
Do you feel anxious when you're not thinking about potential mistakes or dangers and there's nothing in particular worrying you?

I don’t think so, no… not if there’s really nothing in particular on my mind.

I might be a little tense just as a person, I guess, but I wouldn’t describe it as the same kind of anxiety. It’s more that the anxious feeling seems to come with those specific worries. When they’re not there, I can sometimes feel okay.

I hope that makes sense.
Do you have thoughts that repeat over and over in your mind, outside of these specific worries about mistakes or dangers?

Mostly it’s those same kinds of things, I think… like mistakes or something I should have caught.

They repeat a lot, though. I’ll know I checked a number, or I locked the back door, or paid something from the right account, and then the thought just keeps coming back like, “What if you missed something critical?” It feels awful and unwanted, and I can’t seem to make my mind drop it, even when part of me knows I already looked.

I don’t know if that counts as “outside” those worries, exactly. It’s more that those are the thoughts that get stuck. Does that answer it okay?
Do you feel like these repeating thoughts are something you want to think about, or are they unwanted?

No… I don’t want to think about them. They feel very unwanted.

It’s like I’ll try to move on because I know I checked the number, or the door, or the bill, but then the thought comes back anyway—what if I missed something important, what if it causes some kind of disaster. I’m not sitting there choosing to dwell on it, at least I don’t think I am. I’d really rather not have those thoughts at all.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that the right way.
Do you often feel anxious for no particular reason, even when you're not thinking about potential mistakes or dangers?

No, I don’t think so… not really for no reason.

If I’m anxious, it’s usually because something has gotten in my head, like a concern or a “what if.” If there truly isn’t anything like that going on, I might feel a little keyed up sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it the same thing. I don’t want to overstate it. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you ever feel anxious without any specific thought or worry in your mind?

I don’t think so… not in a totally blank way, if that makes sense.

Usually if I feel anxious, there’s some thought attached to it, even if it’s just a quick “what if” that I’m trying not to focus on. I guess I haven’t really noticed anxiety showing up with no worry in my mind at all. But I’m not sure I always catch the thought right away, so… I don’t want to answer it wrong.
Do you think your anxiety would still be a problem if you could somehow be completely sure that all your worries about mistakes or dangers were unfounded?

I think… if I could be completely sure, then no, probably it wouldn’t be the same problem.

That’s the part that gets me, I guess. It’s not like I want to sit around worrying. It’s that my mind keeps saying, what if I missed something critical—like a wrong number in something I released, or the back door not really being locked, or a bill coming out of the wrong account. Even if I checked it, it still feels like there’s this tiny possibility that I caused something awful.

So if I could really know those worries were unfounded, I think I’d feel a lot more okay. I hope that makes sense.
Do you feel like your anxiety is mostly limited to when you're having these specific worries, or does it also show up at other times when you're not thinking about anything in particular?

It’s mostly when those specific worries are there, I think.

I mean, I came in because I keep getting these awful thoughts that I’ve missed something important—like a wrong number in a data release, or that the back door wasn’t really locked, or a bill got paid from the wrong account. And even if I know I checked, my mind just… doesn’t let go of the possibility that I caused some kind of disaster.

So I wouldn’t say it’s just anxiety out of nowhere. It’s tied to those “what if I made a serious mistake” thoughts. I hope I’m explaining that clearly.
Is your anxiety ever present without any of these specific worries or thoughts about mistakes or dangers being in your mind?

I don’t think it’s usually just there by itself, no.

For me it’s more like… the anxiety comes when one of those thoughts grabs on. Like, I’ll think maybe I missed a wrong number in a data release, or maybe the back door wasn’t actually locked, or a bill came out of the wrong account. And even if I know I checked, my mind keeps going, “But what if you didn’t? What if something bad happens because of you?”

So… I guess the worry is usually attached to that kind of thought. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Do you feel like you're often 'on edge' or anxious even when none of those specific worries are on your mind?

I don’t think so… not in a constant way, anyway.

I mean, I can be tense, but when those specific worries aren’t there, I’m not usually sitting around feeling on edge for no reason. At least I haven’t really noticed that. It feels more like it gets stirred up when my mind catches on something.

Does that answer what you mean?
Is there ever a time when you feel anxious without having any of those specific 'what if' thoughts in your mind?

Not really… at least, I don’t think that’s how it usually happens for me.

It’s more that one of those thoughts pops in, and then the anxiety follows. Like I’ll suddenly think, “What if I missed a critical number in that data release?” or “What if the back door wasn’t actually locked?” or “What if that bill came out of the wrong account?” And then even though I know I checked, I can’t seem to let go of the possibility that I caused something really bad.

So I guess the anxious feeling is pretty tied to those thoughts. I hope that makes sense.
Is there ever a time when you feel anxious without any specific thoughts or worries in your mind?

I don’t think so, no… at least not that I can separate out.

It’s usually that the thought comes first — like that I missed a wrong number in a data release, or didn’t really lock the back door, or paid something from the wrong account — and then I get anxious because my mind won’t let go of it. Even if I know I checked, it keeps feeling like maybe I caused some kind of disaster.

I’m sorry if I’m repeating myself. I just mean it doesn’t feel like anxiety out of nowhere so much as it gets attached to those thoughts.
Do you ever experience anxiety that isn't related to one of your specific worries about mistakes or dangers?

No, I don’t think so… not really separate from those things.

It’s usually the same kind of loop: I get this unwanted thought that I missed something important, like a wrong number in a data release, or that I didn’t lock the back door, or maybe I paid a bill from the wrong account. And even if I know I checked, my mind keeps going back to, “But what if you didn’t?” or “What if this causes something awful?”

So I wouldn’t say it’s just general anxiety out of nowhere. It’s more tied to those specific worries about mistakes or something dangerous happening because of me. I hope that’s the right way to explain it.
Is it possible for you to feel anxious without any thoughts or worries present in your mind at that moment?

I don’t think so… or at least, I haven’t noticed it happening that way.

For me it seems to start with the thought first — like, “What if I missed a critical number?” or “What if the back door wasn’t really locked?” or “What if that bill went from the wrong account?” And then I get anxious because I can’t quite let go of the chance that I caused something awful, even if I already checked.

I’m sorry, I know I’ve probably said that a few times. I just mean the anxiety usually has one of those worries attached to it.
Is it ever possible for you to feel anxious without having any of those specific 'what if' thoughts in your mind at the same time?

I don’t think it really happens without them, no. I mean, if I feel anxious, there’s almost always one of those thoughts sitting there with it — like that I missed a critical number in something at work, or that the back door wasn’t actually locked, or that I paid something from the wrong account.

Even when I know I checked, it’s like my mind won’t accept it and keeps saying, “What if you caused a disaster?” That’s the part I came in for, really. Sorry, I hope I’m answering what you’re asking.
Is it ever possible for you to feel anxious without any thoughts or worries present in your mind at that moment?

I don’t think so, no… at least not that I can tell.

The anxiety seems to come with the thought. I came in because I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical—like a wrong number in a data release, or the back door being unlocked, or a bill coming out of the wrong account. And even when I know I checked, my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I caused some kind of disaster.

I’m sorry if I’m repeating myself. I just don’t really notice the anxious feeling by itself without one of those worries attached.
